catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner codebase, commands, skills, and governance engine.
analysis_limits: No dynamic execution traces available during static analysis
Step implementations under cas_runner pipeline inferred from runner and governance modules

system_map.overview: The CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner coordinates agentic skills and commands to maintain architectural alignment, automate governance transitions, evaluate compliance, and reconcile artifacts through an extensible pipeline.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step agentic workflows and pipeline execution across development cycles.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles and resolves merges between architecture specifications, code changes, and generated assets.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Evaluates transition prerequisites and executes valid governance state transitions across architecture states.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates system state against defined architectural constraints, producing structured findings.

orchestration.description: Pipeline execution is driven sequentially via FlowRunner while individual governance operations and skill invocations use a declarative registry and state-transition model.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to multiple LLM backends with parameter normalization and error handling.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Enables deterministic evaluation, unit testing, and offline execution of agentic components.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Emits telemetry spans and trace context across agent runs and governance validations.

state_and_memory.description: Governance inventory, metrics, findings, and actions typed via Pydantic models and stored in repository artifacts.
In-memory execution context mutated and passed sequentially through pipeline step runners.

patterns.name: Provider-Agnostic LLM Facade

tool_protocols.notes: Abstracts provider-level completion and tool calling under unified client interfaces.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents vendor lock-in and isolates agent reasoning logic from provider API churn.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Direct wrapper abstraction over LiteLLM eliminates redundant driver code.

patterns.summary: Encapsulates LLM interactions behind a unified client interface to ensure provider portability and uniform call semantics across agent tasks.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent business logic from specific model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) while standardizing call contracts.
patterns.context: Used across all runner steps and governance modules requiring LLM generation or structured output parsing.
forces: Different model providers feature varying API schemas and error structures
Pipeline components need uniform invocation mechanics without vendor coupling
patterns.solution: Wrap LiteLLM into a dedicated client class that exposes uniform methods for prompt execution, structured response generation, and error mapping.
implementation_signals: Direct dependency on litellm in pyproject.toml

evidence.note: Provides consistent invocation wrapper around LiteLLM for agent steps.

benefits: Zero code changes required in agent logic when swapping models
Centralized configuration for retries, timeouts, and token metrics
costs: Leaky abstractions when provider-specific features (e.g., custom tool schemas) are needed
failure_modes: LiteLLM version mismatches leading to unexpected translation errors across esoteric providers

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to any Python agent runner requiring model flexibility without altering workflow contracts.

patterns.name: Deterministic Mock Evaluation Harness

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows CI pipelines and governance tests to run deterministically with zero token costs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Static mocks prioritize deterministic verification over synthetic model simulation.

patterns.summary: Provides a drop-in mock LLM client to execute agent pipelines deterministically in CI/CD without network or model flakiness.
patterns.intent: Enable fast, zero-cost, and deterministic end-to-end testing of agentic workflows and governance decision flows.
patterns.context: Implemented alongside the production LLM client to support offline unit tests, regression suites, and CI pipelines.
forces: Live LLM calls in CI are nondeterministic, slow, and incur cost
Agent pipelines must be validated end-to-end including state transitions and schema validation
patterns.solution: Implement a `MockLLMClient` that implements the client contract and returns predefined responses or deterministic schemas based on inputs.

evidence.note: Implements deterministic mock LLM interface for testing runner flows.

benefits: Zero token cost during continuous integration runs
Guaranteed repeatability for regression test suites
costs: Mock responses must be manually updated when prompt schemas evolve
failure_modes: Mocks drift from real LLM output distributions, masking hallucination or formatting failures

patterns.reuse_notes: Essential pattern for any production agent system needing automated CI validation without live provider dependencies.

patterns.name: Declarative Agent Command Registry

tool_protocols.notes: Commands specify declarative execution configurations and bindings for skills.

optimisation_targets.notes: Exposes agentic capabilities as modular, reproducible CLI and agent commands.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Declarative TOML definitions allow humans and agents to trigger consistent multi-step tasks.

patterns.summary: Externalizes agent task specifications and skills into declarative TOML manifests in the repository.
patterns.intent: Standardize how agent capabilities (planning, specifying, analyzing, migrating) are defined, shared, and triggered.
patterns.context: Located in `.agents/commands/` and `.agents/skills/` to configure speckit lifecycle operations.
forces: Hardcoded CLI commands make agent workflows rigid and difficult to configure per project
Agents and human developers need identical interfaces to invoke standardized architectural skills
patterns.solution: Define modular TOML specifications for each command (e.g. `speckit.plan.toml`, `speckit.analyze.toml`, `speckit.brownfield.migrate.toml`) mapping prompts, inputs, and skill dependencies.

evidence.note: Defines declarative command contract for the planning agentic skill.
Defines declarative specification for analysis workflows.

benefits: Self-documenting agent interfaces visible directly in version control
Skills can be composed and parameterized across brownfield and greenfield workflows
costs: Proliferation of TOML files requiring governance and sync tooling
failure_modes: Skill directory structure drifting from command definitions resulting in missing command targets

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt whenever a system exposes multiple agentic skills that need versioning alongside the codebase.

patterns.name: Finite-State Governance Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions evaluate preconditions against domain models.

optimisation_targets.notes: Constrains autonomous agents from executing illegal architectural state transitions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit state transitions strictly gate autonomous agent outputs before persistence.

patterns.summary: Constrains agent-driven architecture changes using a TransitionRegistry and state transition engine that validates precondition constraints.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents or automated runs from transitioning architectural states or closing compliance issues without meeting formal criteria.
patterns.context: Implemented in `cas_runner.governance` to manage governance actions and artifact statuses.
forces: Unconstrained LLM outputs can declare architecture tasks 'complete' prematurely
Transitions between architecture stages require formal invariant checking
patterns.solution: Define a `TransitionRegistry` mapping valid source and target states, and use a `GovernanceActionEngine` to inspect preconditions prior to applying actions.
implementation_signals: GovernanceActionEngine executing transitions over GovernanceAction domain entities

evidence.note: Encapsulates valid state transitions and gating rules for governance changes.
Provides typed schema definitions for transitions and state tracking.

benefits: Deterministic boundary preventing hallucinated state changes
Clear audit trail for compliance and health calculations
costs: Every new governance phase requires registering formal transitions
failure_modes: Overly rigid transition rules causing deadlock in automated remediation runs

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful in any agentic system where agents have mutation permissions over production metadata or regulatory artifacts.

patterns.name: Reconciliation Agentic Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Synthesizes conflicts and produces ResolutionResult models.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates conflict resolution while maintaining architecture design invariants.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Delegates complex non-trivial artifact reconciliation to an LLM-assisted merger component.

patterns.summary: Employs an LLM-assisted reconciliation component to merge diverging architectural specifications and code artifacts into a cohesive state.
patterns.intent: Resolve discrepancies between human-authored architectural decisions and agent-generated implementation models.
forces: Multi-branch agent edits and parallel human modifications create structural schema conflicts
Standard git merge drivers fail on semantic JSON/YAML architectural projections
patterns.solution: Implement `AgenticMerger` that leverages LLM contextual understanding to synthesize conflicts and return a structured `ResolutionResult`.

evidence.note: Performs semantic reconciliation between conflicting architectural states.
Encapsulates merge resolution outcome and metadata.

benefits: Reduces human toil in resolving non-trivial semantic diffs
Preserves design intent across asynchronous updates
costs: Requires strict post-resolution verification to prevent semantic regression
failure_modes: Silently dropping edge-case constraints during merge generation

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to structured document reconciliation, specification alignment, or AST merging pipelines.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline Flow Runner

tool_protocols.notes: Coordinates execution steps sequentially passing contextual state.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides predictable sequential step execution with structured error boundaries.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Linear step chaining is favored over autonomous reactive looping to ensure predictability.

patterns.summary: Executes discrete agentic and verification steps sequentially through an orchestrator passing updated execution context.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-stage architectural assessment and generation tasks with deterministic ordering and failure handling.
forces: Complex agent tasks require clear ordering (e.g. assess -> plan -> specify -> implement)
Uncontrolled agent self-looping can lead to infinite execution cycles and high token spend
patterns.solution: Define `FlowRunner` to execute defined steps in strict sequence, feeding outputs of earlier stages as inputs to subsequent stages.
implementation_signals: CLI command dispatching flows in src/cas_runner/cli.py

evidence.note: Coordinates execution of workflow steps and accumulates execution context.
Serves as the entrypoint invoking FlowRunner for CLI commands.

benefits: Easy to reason about and trace failure origins
Simplifies resumption and checkpointing across steps
costs: Less adaptive than dynamic multi-agent conversation graphs
failure_modes: Failure in an upstream step unconditionally stalls downstream processing unless explicit fallback steps exist

patterns.reuse_notes: Foundation for deterministic agentic pipelines where task stages follow known workflows.

patterns.name: Schema-Enforced Domain Contracts

tool_protocols.notes: Pydantic and jsonschema define and validate inputs and outputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees that all agent outputs adhere strictly to typed domain schemas before mutation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strict schema contracts eliminate hallucinated payload shapes while leaving generation open.

patterns.summary: Enforces strict Pydantic and JSON Schema models for all governance entities, ensuring agent outputs are validated prior to consumption.
patterns.intent: Eliminate malformed, incomplete, or hallucinated payloads generated by LLM steps before modifying repository state.
forces: LLMs frequently omit required attributes or produce inconsistent data structures
Downstream visualization and health calculators expect strongly-typed models
patterns.solution: Define comprehensive Pydantic domain models (`ComplianceFinding`, `GovernanceInventory`, `GovernanceHealth`, `GovernanceRisks`) and reject or repair payloads that fail schema validation.
implementation_signals: Models in src/cas_runner/governance/models.py deriving from Pydantic BaseModel
Dependencies on pydantic>=2.12.5 and jsonschema>=4.22.0 in pyproject.toml

evidence.note: Defines rigid contracts for state, action payloads, and compliance results.

benefits: Prevents runtime TypeErrors across downstream consumers
Provides unambiguous parsing targets for LLM structured output functions
costs: Schema changes require coordinated updates across prompt instructions and model definitions
failure_modes: Strict validation rejections causing execution halts when an LLM produces equivalent but unexpected formats

patterns.reuse_notes: Universal pattern for agent systems requiring reliable interactions between probabilistic models and deterministic engines.

patterns.name: Telemetry-Observable Agent Steps

tool_protocols.notes: OpenTelemetry hooks instrument flow runner steps and LLM calls.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables end-to-end tracing and debugging of multi-step agent runs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardized OTel spans provide uniform observability across heterogeneous agent actions.

patterns.summary: Instruments pipeline execution and agent interactions with OpenTelemetry to track latency, token usage, and step errors.
patterns.intent: Provide comprehensive visibility into the latency, cost, and error boundaries of agentic runs.
patterns.context: Integrated via OpenTelemetry SDK dependencies configured in the runner runtime.
forces: Multi-step agent pipelines suffer from opacity when failures occur inside nested LLM calls
Debugging cost spikes and slow steps requires distributed trace context
patterns.solution: Integrate OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry-api` and `opentelemetry-sdk`) to wrap runner executions and step transitions with traceable spans.
implementation_signals: opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk in pyproject.toml dependencies

evidence.note: Encapsulates metric records carrying trace context.

benefits: Standardized export of execution metrics to backends like Jaeger or Prometheus
Granular attribution of errors to specific agent prompt steps
costs: Instrumentation overhead in step dispatch logic
failure_modes: Context propagation drops between asynchronous threads or child processes

patterns.reuse_notes: Directly applicable to any production agent system to satisfy enterprise observability requirements.

patterns.name: CI-Driven Steering Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Workflows trigger agent sync and projection generation routines.

optimisation_targets.notes: Keeps architectural documentation, diagrams, and governance health continuously in sync with codebase evolution.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Event-driven CI triggers execute bounded agent projection generation on git commits.

patterns.summary: Leverages continuous integration workflows to trigger agentic projection tasks that synchronize architecture docs, diagrams, and health dashboards.
patterns.intent: Maintain continuous synchronization between evolving code and architectural governance projections without manual documentation overhead.
patterns.context: Configured across GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/` (e.g. `cas-build-steering-projection.yml`, `cas-continuous-architecture.yml`).
forces: Architecture documentation and C4 diagrams quickly drift from actual code without automated synchronization
Running continuous background agent daemons is costly and complex
patterns.solution: Trigger agentic projection routines (such as `cas-drawio-generator` and `cas-sync-archgov-reviews`) on pull requests and commits using GitHub Actions.

evidence.note: Automates projection generation on repository events.
Triggers continuous architecture analysis and governance validation.

benefits: Zero human intervention required to publish updated architecture portals and diagrams
Architectural health metrics are continuously validated as part of branch checks
costs: GitHub Actions runner minutes and external API token consumption during frequent commits
failure_modes: Merge conflicts occurring when CI pushes projected documentation back into the source branch

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal pattern for continuous architecture, living documentation, and automated governance platforms.

anti_patterns.name: Unconstrained Autonomous Reconciliation
symptoms: Allowing AgenticMerger to commit resolved changes directly without AST or schema re-validation
Accepting resolution summaries without explicit automated diff inspection

where_observed.note: Semantic resolution risks subtle behavioral shifts if unvalidated downstream.

impact: Subtle architectural regressions or omitted constraints in merged output
False sense of compliance when the model resolves syntax conflicts but alters semantic intent
suggested_remediation: Enforce automated lint, schema validation, and test suite execution on all AgenticMerger outputs before applying state transitions.
Require human sign-off on non-trivial architectural diffs exceeding risk thresholds.

anti_patterns.name: Untracked Mock Fidelity Drift
symptoms: MockLLMClient outputs remaining static while prompt specifications or system models evolve
Tests passing cleanly with mock fixtures while production runs fail schema validation against live models

where_observed.note: Mock returns fixed structures that may decouple from evolving prompt requirements.

impact: Green CI pipelines masking regressions in prompt engineering or model instruction parsing
Sudden deployment failures when live LLMs deviate from outdated mock formats
suggested_remediation: Validate mock responses directly against the Pydantic domain models in the test suite.
Implement periodic scheduled integration tests that run a subset of flows against live models to verify mock parity.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Command specifications and skills in `.agents/commands/` externalize prompts and operational intents into structured files rather than raw inline strings.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Decoupling prompts from Python execution logic enables prompt tuning and auditing without modifying runner code.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Enforcing state machine checks in `GovernanceActionEngine` and schema constraints in `models.py` before any state transition can take effect.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Ensures agents operate strictly within verified bounds regardless of LLM generation randomness.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrating OpenTelemetry instrumentation across runner workflows to track spans, metric traces, and error events.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Provides standard distributed tracing compatibility for agent execution runs.
